roadmap.goal: Slice 01 of ADO Story 6070: every CI job, the Docker frontend stage and the maintainer's shell take Node from .nvmrc, pnpm refuses a wrong Node, and a guard test fails CI if a literal Node version comes back. Acceptance: the Node-family tests in .github/scripts/toolchain-pins.test.mjs go from skipped to GREEN (the compliant tree, 14 seeded drifts, and the real repository); pnpm-family tests stay skipped for slice 02; frontend pnpm test + pnpm build stay green under the .nvmrc Node.

validation.reviewer: orchestrator (inline, mirroring the bug-6054 precedent for a mechanical, fully specified change)
validation.notes: No architect dispatch: DESIGN was skipped by the user and D1-D11 plus DISTILL T1-T5 in feature-delta.md prescribe every edit. The acceptance tests were reviewed and approved at the end of DISTILL. Every DISTILL Node-family test maps to a step (01-01: tests 3-17; 01-02: test 1); pnpm-family tests (2, 18-25) belong to slice 02 and are deliberately out of this roadmap. Local fnm setup (AC2.1-2.2) was done and verified by the orchestrator before this roadmap, at the user's request, since it touches the maintainer's own shell config rather than the repository.

user_decisions: Dockerfile ARG NODE_VERSION with no default (D2)
engines strict, fnm set up locally first (D3, D4)
SSOT proof via throwaway features/ probe branch (D5) - a push, so it waits for the user
out_of_scope: Probe branch push and main push - orchestrator, after user review

files_to_modify: .github/scripts/toolchain-pins.test.mjs (unskip the Node-family tests only: test 3 and the NODE_DRIFTS loop; the two real-repository tests and PNPM_DRIFTS stay skipped)
criteria: All 15 listed tests GREEN; the real-repository tests and the 8 pnpm drifts remain skipped; generate-version tests still GREEN.
Each seeded drift yields exactly one violation, with family 'node', the rule id, the repo-relative file path (forward slashes) and 1-based line where the test expects one.
When .nvmrc is missing or malformed, rules that compare against it (engines-node-mismatch) stay silent rather than adding a second violation.

No dependencies: node: built-ins only. YAML and Dockerfiles are read line by line. Scans .github/**/*.yml|yaml, Dockerfile, .nvmrc, and the two projects' package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml under the given root; a file that does not exist is skipped unless a rule requires it.
__SCAFFOLD__ export removed. Every violation carries a message that says what to write instead (e.g. use node-version-file: '.nvmrc').
RED captured first: with the tests unskipped against the scaffold they fail on AssertionError.
steps.implementation_notes: Match the style of .github/scripts/generate-version.mjs (tabs, ESM, small named functions). Structure the rules so slice 02 can add the pnpm family without touching the Node rules (e.g. a list of rule functions each returning violations). Rule details are D9 and T1-T5 in feature-delta.md: engines.node must equal `${nvmrc major}.x`; engine-strict means `engineStrict: true` in that project's pnpm-workspace.yaml; the Dockerfile must declare `ARG NODE_VERSION` (no `=`) before its first FROM, and its node stage must use `node:${NODE_VERSION}`; ci_docker.yml must pass `--build-arg NODE_VERSION=$(cat .nvmrc)`; ci.yml push.paths must list `.nvmrc`; .nvmrc must match /^\d+(\.\d+){0,2}$/. Comments only where the why is not readable from code, in plain language, no internal references (project CLAUDE.md). Commit: `feat(toolchain): guard reports Node versions written outside .nvmrc`

steps.name: Pin the guard's near-miss behaviour (mutation remediation)
steps.description: StrykerJS on toolchain-pins.mjs scored 74.85% (378 killed / 127 survived) against the 80% per-feature gate. Survivors are dominated by regex anchor/whitespace mutants and step-scoping conditionals that no fixture exercises: every fixture spells each construct exactly one way. Add tests that specify the behaviour at those edges; production code stays frozen unless a test exposes a real defect.
steps.scenario_name: near-miss spellings are judged by what they mean, not how they are written
criteria: Mutation score on .github/scripts/toolchain-pins.mjs >= 80% with the same Stryker setup (command runner over node --test).

New tests describe behaviour a maintainer would care about (comments are not pins; registry-prefixed images are pins; engineStrict false is off; a neighbouring step's version is not the pnpm step's; blank/comment lines inside a with: block; missing .github directory; formatting variants such as extra spaces or quote styles), not mutant-shaped assertions.
Any survivor judged equivalent is listed with a one-line reason in the report.
If a new test exposes a real defect, stop and report it rather than changing production code.
steps.implementation_notes: Commit: `test(toolchain): pin how the guard reads comments and formatting variants`.

steps.name: The guard reads past trailing YAML comments
steps.description: Found by mutation remediation: a trailing `# comment` on a YAML line changes the guard's verdict. `with:  # inputs` on a pnpm step hides any `version:` under it (a pin slips through); `engineStrict: true # why` reads as off; `- ".nvmrc"  # why` in ci.yml paths reads as not listed.
steps.scenario_name: a trailing comment on a YAML line does not change what the guard sees
red_to_green_tests: reports a pnpm version under a with: line that carries a trailing comment
accepts engineStrict: true followed by a comment
accepts .nvmrc in the CI trigger paths followed by a comment
criteria: The three tests above fail first against current code, then pass.
Trailing YAML comments (whitespace then # to end of line, outside quotes) are ignored when matching YAML lines; a # inside a quoted value is not a comment.
The flow-style `with: { package_json_file: ... }` false alarm stays out of scope; note it as a known limit in a comment only if the code would otherwise mislead a reader.
Whole suite green; mutation score re-measured and still >= 80%.
steps.implementation_notes: Commit: `fix(toolchain): the guard reads past trailing YAML comments`.
